articles.title_orig: Neurable One Review: The Brain-Scanning Headphones That Helped Me Stay Focused
articles.title_zh: Neurable One Review: The Brain-Scanning Headphones That Helped Me Stay Focused
articles.content_orig:
The cans hide a wearable EEG that tracks your attention.
I've always been fascinated by the inner workings of the human mind , and I've tested plenty of brain gadgets in my time. Sadly, all of them have been so clunky that they can only really be worn in the privacy of your own home. At least, that was the case. The Neurable One actually buries its brain-scanning technology into a pair of beefy over-ear headphones. It's designed to keep an eye on your focus levels and attention while you work, or meditate, wherever you are.
The company describes it as a "fitness tracker for your brain," so when your attention starts to drift, the headphones will remind you to keep your focus where it needs to be. And, if things continue to go wayward, you'll be advised to take a break and come back fresh rather than burning out halfway through the day. In that regard, it's been fascinating to see how the system thinks my brain operates on a regular basis.
The Neurable One is cheaper than its predecessors and its competitors, and Neurable has improved its software platform. If there's a downside, it's that as much as I've loved my time with them, it's hard to think anyone other than nerds like me will want to use them.
Neurable spun out of a project from the University of Michigan in 2015, with the goal of building Brain Computer Interfaces (BCIs) and algorithms to interpret that data. The focus is on cognitive performance as there's plenty of military and civilian applications for the technology. Despite the name, Neurable One is actually the third pair of EEG headphones the company has made. In 2024, it partnered with Master & Dynamic on the MW75 Neuro, and a year later the Neuro LT, a lighter version of the same product addressing user comfort issues. This time out, Neurable is going it alone without the backing of any fancy audio brands.
At a glance, you'll struggle to notice much difference between this and its predecessors, as any variances are mostly aesthetic tweaks. Button placements are the same, but they're now pill-shaped rather than the circles found on the older models. The logo on the earcups has changed from M&D's icon to Neurable's signature brainwave, and there are fewer vents. In fact, the biggest difference is the loss of the cantilevered armatures joining the headband to the earcups, which have been replaced with standard hardware here.
It's a similar story inside the body as well; the Neurable One is more or less equipped with the same gear as before. You'll get the same 40mm Beryllium drivers, Bluetooth 5.2, AAC and aptX, albeit with six microphones — down from the eight on the MW75 Neuro. As before, each earcup has a series of dry-fit EEG sensors woven into the earpads which sit around your ear.
Neurable's pitch is to help people gain deeper insights into their own cognitive performance through the day. It contends that, much like the rest of our body, our minds have enough fuel to get us through the day, but not at full-tilt, full-pelt output. The company says it's a better idea to, when your attention and focus starts to wane, take a break ahead of you burning out. Neurable argues that spending a quick five minutes staring out of the window is better than getting a headache and not functioning for an hour.
Strap the headphones on at the start of the day and the system will keep an eye on how you're doing. Do this over a period of days, or weeks, and you'll get a sense of where your focus is at its highest and lowest. You can then adjust your working patterns to suit those stats. The Neurable One works equally well when you're meditating or relaxing, giving you insights as to how and when your mind rests.
One of my eternal gripes with a lot of wearable EEGs (and other fabric sensors more broadly) is that the sensor pads are often fussy. They often don't work at all if they're bone dry and the skin they're in contact with is dry as well, which frustrates me. I've regularly had to gently dab the pads with cold water before running a washcloth across my forehead to dampen it. But, if the skin and pads are too wet, you'll be given a warning to dry both out, which slows you down even further. Thankfully, the Neurable One's dry-fit sensors worked from the get-go more or less every time I've used them. Every now and again, I'll be asked to push my (short) hair away from around my ears to improve the connection, but it's a world away from other products in the same field that I've tested.
Setup is a breeze, and the process of beginning your first session is relatively effortless, as is the daily routine you're expected to fall into. That begins with a check in at the start of the day, closing your eyes and triggering a 60-second scan of your brain. You'll get a dashboard containing your scores, with a comparison to the day before to see if things got better or worse. If you had a rough night, or if there's a lot going on, you can journal some notes on the same pane.
What's far more interesting and useful are the Insights and Improve sections, which tell you both what to do to manage your cognitive load right now, and how to boost it. The former suggests that you delay big decisions, not starting jobs that need a lot of attention and grouping small, repetitive tasks together. The latter asks you to go for a quick walk in the sun, go sit in another room away from your computer for five minutes or to write down all of the things sitting in your mental cache. Once done, you can run another check-in to see if that's made any improvement.
If I'm honest, I was having a busy day at the start of a busy week, and felt snowed under by all of the projects on my desk. (In fact, my biggest issue, throughout testing these headphones, was that my Cognitive Load was always problematically high. It's almost as if working in journalism and juggling hundreds of projects all at once is somehow a problem.) The app told me that I was running low, but said I should walk up and down my stairs for a few minutes and then come back and check again. And, wouldn't you know, it actually did improve both my score and my ability to get stuff done for the rest of the morning.
Most days, I would set the EEG running at 9AM or so and not take them off until 12 or 1PM. The app will keep track of how well it thinks you're concentrating, letting you see that as a real time figure on screen. If it detects your focus beginning to drift, it'll rouse you back, but after a while, if you still struggle to concentrate, it'll advise you to take a short break. One thing I don't like is the way the system prods you to get back on track: When it thinks your focus is waning, you'll get a ping played in your ear as a sort of "come on, pay attention" trigger.
It's a harsh noise, and one that would distract me as often as it did help me drift back toward focus. You can shut off this guidance in the app, but I persevered with them even when it put me in mind of a '70s kung fu B-movie where the protagonist is asked to build a house of cards while being pelted with rotten fruit. Regularly, I'd be halfway through writing a line in what I'd describe as a flow state and then I'd get pinged, knocking me off my train of thought.
But the more I used the headphones, the more I was able to see when the system said I was doing well and what caused slips. It became an increasingly positive feedback loop where I'd scrub through the timeline of my morning to see what I was doing when my focus was high.
As for audio quality, it's clear the company has tried to sail close to Master & Dynamic's promise of warm bass and clear treble. There's a wonderful atmosphere to the sound that makes you feel like you're in the room when it was recorded. One of my favourite tracks to test headphones with is "Finale" from the Tron: Legacy soundtrack where you can hear the horn player's breath. Wearing these, I was equally delighted to feel the rumble of the kettle drums pushing the air to my ear as they crescendoed.
The downside of Neu

articles.title_orig: Dead racehorse found in dumpster days after running in prestigious race: "Distressing and completely unacceptable"
articles.title_zh: Dead racehorse found in dumpster days after running in prestigious race: "Distressing and completely unacceptable"
articles.content_orig:
The dead body of Melbourne Cup horse So You Are was found in a waste facility in Sydney less than two weeks after competing in the most prestigious event in Australian horse racing.
The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported Tuesday that racing stewards were investigating after a construction worker saw a dead horse in a dumpster at a licensed waste center and posted a video on Facebook.
Trainer Bjorn Baker had released a statement Monday saying So You Are died following a severe bout of colic. The 5-year-old gelding was rushed to a specialist equine hospital for emergency veterinary treatment but couldn't be saved.
Baker posted an update Tuesday after discovering So You Are hadn't been properly buried.
"Like everyone who has seen the footage, I am deeply distressed by the handling of So You Are's remains," Baker said in a statement. "He was a much-loved horse, and he deserved to be treated with dignity and respect after his death."
"I understand the specialist hospital facility REC Equine Specialists are investigating the circumstances, and I expect a full explanation of what occurred," he added. "My thoughts remain with the Ramsey family [owners], and with all my staff, for whom this has compounded an already devastating loss."
So You Are placed eighth in the Melbourne Cup on Nov. 3, with Point of Law winning the 166th running of the 2-mile classic.
REC Equine Specialists managing partner Dr. Jonathan Lumsden issued a statement saying So You Are had been "humanely euthanized under anesthesia" after receiving emergency treatment.
"After his death, So You Are was collected by our contracted service provider and taken to a licensed landfill. He should have been promptly and respectfully buried," Lumsden said. "What happened was unacceptable and disrespectful to So You Are and to everyone who cared for him. We are deeply sorry."
Lumsden said he was working with the service provider and the state's horse racing authority, Racing NSW, to establish what went wrong and to put in processes to ensure it never happens again.
"So You Are was in our care. We did not carry out the burial ourselves, but we chose the provider and the arrangements, and we take full responsibility for that," he said. "We should have known exactly how horses were handled after leaving our hospital, and we did not. That process is not good enough, and it must change.
"No owner should have to go through what So You Are's connections have experienced this week."
Waste management company Cleanaway, which runs the landfill, told national broadcaster ABC the horse's body was moved to a permitted area of the site.
"Cleanaway's Lucas Heights landfill is licensed to accept and dispose of animal carcasses," a spokesperson told ABC. "The horse carcass delivered to the facility arrived in a small tipper truck, which is not permitted on the landfill tipping face for safety reasons. In accordance with established procedures, the carcass was transferred into a skip bin to enable its safe disposal at the landfill."
Racing NSW said So You Are was being held temporarily, awaiting burial, when the video was recorded.
"These images are distressing for all involved and for all of us who care deeply about our horses," Racing NSW said in a statement. "The way in which So You Are's body was left is distressing and completely unacceptable. So You Are deserved to be treated with dignity and respect."
The state's racing regulator said under industry guidelines — now under review — a licensed landfill was the preferred option for animals that have been euthanized because of the chemicals involved in the process.
"That burial, however, should have occurred in a timely and respectful manner," the statement continued. "If through the course of our ongoing investigation any wrongdoing is found, Racing NSW will not hesitate to take appropriate action."
Australian politician Emma Hurst called the news "absolutely heartbreaking," but not surprising, ABC reported.
"This horse has been treated as though he is nothing more than a piece of rubbish," she said. "To be completely honest, I'm not entirely surprised. We've had complaints about the racing industry for the entire eight years that I have been in parliament."

Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) said on Tuesday that its experimental cancer vaccine, Galinpepimut-S (GPS), significantly improved overall survival in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML), with the biotech firm eyeing a potential regulatory filing in the first half of next year.
The company announced that its pivotal Phase 3 Regal trial met its primary goal, with GPS reducing the risk of death by 41% compared with the best available treatment (BAT). The trial also showed a median overall survival (OS) of 24 months, compared with 14.7 months for those receiving BAT.
See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox
Sellas said the results were statistically significant, with a hazard ratio of 0.59 and a p-value of 0.035.
SLS shares were up 7.1% pre-market, before trading was halted.
Sellas is expected to meet with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to discuss an accelerated filing strategy and advance preparations for a Biologics License Application (BLA) submission in the first half of 2027.
"Given the significant unmet need in this patient population, we look forward to engaging with the FDA to discuss the results and the regulatory path forward, with the goal of making this therapy available to patients as rapidly as possible," CEO Angelos Stergiou said.
The 126-patient study evaluated GPS as maintenance therapy for AML patients in their second or later remission who could not undergo a stem cell transplant.
GPS, licensed from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, targets WT1, a protein found in multiple types of cancers. GPS is designed to help the immune system identify and attack leukemia cells.
Sellas said the treatment was generally well tolerated, with no new safety concerns. Most treatment-related side effects were mild or moderate, with reactions mainly at the injection site.
The company announced last month that the Regal trial had reached its prespecified 80th event, the milestone required to begin its final analysis. Sellas is now conducting further analyses of the results, which will be presented at an upcoming major medical conference and submitted for publication in a peer-reviewed medical journal.

articles.title_orig: Xbox 360 rigged with explosives detonates at rival repair shop in Brazil, injuring two people
articles.title_zh: Xbox 360 rigged with explosives detonates at rival repair shop in Brazil, injuring two people
articles.content_orig:
Police in Brazil arrested a 39-year-old businessman after an explosive Xbox 360 damaged a competing repair shop.
Brazilian reports confirm the console was an Xbox 360. Police suspect a competing repair shop owner arranged the attack.
A repair shop owner in Brazil has been arrested after an Xbox 360 containing explosives detonated at a competing electronics store. The incident occurred on October 23 in Santo André, near São Paulo. Two people suffered minor injuries, while the explosion damaged the store’s ceiling and furniture.
According to Brazilian media outlet g1, the console was delivered to the Goody Store by a motorcycle courier who believed it needed modification. The courier reportedly had no knowledge of the explosives. The store owner placed the Xbox 360 inside a drawer, where it detonated later that evening.
Empresário é preso suspeito de enviar videogame com explosivos que detonaram em loja de eletrônicos de Santo André, Grande SP https://t.co/EqXSlkM1J9 #g1 pic.twitter.com/H3naAgNzlV
— g1 (@g1) November 16, 2026
Investigators discovered two explosive charges inside the console, although only one detonated. Police believe the device was intended to kill the store owner. The explosion caused structural damage, while the owner and another person suffered minor injuries, including burns.
Police arrested 39-year-old Everton Yoshizumi Lima on November 14. He owns three electronics businesses, including two on the same street where the targeted shop had recently opened. Investigators suspect the attack was motivated by commercial competition.
Security camera recordings captured the delivery and the subsequent explosion. The footage also shows an employee examining the console before storing it. The employee reportedly noticed a strong smell of glue but had already left the shop before the explosion.
Lima is being investigated for attempted aggravated murder. His defense denies any involvement and plans to challenge his detention. Police are also investigating reports of earlier sabotage at the same location, although those incidents have not been linked to the suspect.

articles.title_orig: Nike lays out financial goals ahead of first investor day in 9 years
articles.title_zh: Nike lays out financial goals ahead of first investor day in 9 years
articles.content_orig:
Nike said Tuesday ahead of its first investor day in nine years that it was reaffirming its 2027 financial guidance.
The retailer also laid out a financial framework and said that by the end of fiscal 2031 it's targeting approximately $5 billion in incremental revenue growth from fiscal year 2027, operating margins of 12% to 14% and adjusted earnings per share of $3.00 to $3.50. The company said higher-quality revenue, gross margin expansion and productivity improvements would help it reach its goals.
Nike's 2027 financial guidance includes expectations for revenue to decline in the high-single-digit range, an adjusted operating margin of approximately 6%, and adjusted EPS of $1.15 to $1.35.
The company also introduced a strategy it's calling Full Stride Ahead, which the company said aims "to get closer to athletes and focus resources on the greatest opportunities for long-term growth."
"We're concentrating our resources where we have the greatest potential to win," Nike CEO Elliott Hill said in a statement. "We're also changing how we operate — delivering breakthrough products, building deeper local connections and moving faster to capture demand. Together, these actions are designed to return NIKE to sustainable, profitable growth."
Nike said it would focus on performance sports and sportswear opportunities "with the greatest potential for long-term growth," and said its five priority sports would be running, training, global football, basketball and outdoor.
Nike is holding an investor day at its Oregon headquarters Tuesday as the company aims to prove to investors that its turnaround strategy is yielding success after a yearslong slump.
Last month, the company reported mixed fiscal first-quarter results as it announced a restructuring plan, including layoffs that it said would start next year. It's the company's third round of layoffs to be announced this year.
Nike's net income and revenue both fell during the most recent period compared with a year ago, and the company said it expects revenue to decline by a high single-digit percentage in fiscal 2027.
The new strategy, dubbed Pace, focuses on the company's supply chain and reorganizing into three geographies. Nike said the turnaround plan is expected to deliver roughly $2.5 billion in savings through fiscal 2031.
Nike has been seeing significant sustained declines in its China market, where revenue last quarter dropped 26%. Experts have said the company is losing relevance in the country, while Nike has said it's actively working to win over younger consumers.
At the same time, Nike announced last quarter that it's creating a new global campus in India as part of its new growth strategy, hoping the country will help boost its performance. The company said it was remaining focused on China even as it begins to build out its India presence.
CEO Elliott Hill's turnaround strategy includes improving different parts of the business at different rates based on priority. While it's seen some signs of progress in the North America business, Hill has said that performance isn't enough to offset the pressures on the company elsewhere, including internationally.
The Nike consumer has also been under increased macroeconomic pressure as geopolitical tensions mount and inflation rises.
Shares of Nike have fallen 50% over the past two years.

articles.title_orig: New Zealand tricks and annual leave - the lengths fans are going to for GTA 6
articles.title_zh: New Zealand tricks and annual leave - the lengths fans are going to for GTA 6
articles.content_orig:
Grand Theft Auto 6 will feature a playable female character for the first time since the 2D games
Grand Theft Auto fans have waited 13 long years for the latest edition of the game to be released - and going to extreme lengths to be ready for its launch.
GTA 6 will be released at midnight on Thursday - and Victoria Evans, from West Sussex, is not leaving anything to chance.
She has her alarm set for 05:00 GMT, and has a day off booked. She says she put the game's release on her leave request form which was approved, she told BBC News, despite the fact her boss "doesn't know what GTA 6 is".
She's far from the only one. For the game's launch day, HR software company BrightHR , external looked at absence data from more than 1.2 million employees from 70,000 businesses across the UK.
It found GTA was mentioned in 4.6% of time-off requests by employees. Throughout November and December, it said an estimated 83,000 days had been booked off for the game.
And booking leave is only one of the ways fans are making sure for the big day. Others are buying a new console to play it on or even pretending they're halfway around the world to get early access.
Market intelligence firm Sensor Tower estimates , external GTA 6 has already generated $1.18bn (Â£894m) from 12 million pre-orders - although Rockstar has not confirmed this.
Despite the option to preload the 212GB game, Jennifer Holmes, chief executive of the London Internet Exchange, said several UK internet providers including BT and Virgin Media had "increased capacity in anticipation of higher demand" ahead of launch.
GTA 6 - all you need to know about Rockstar's blockbuster game
Gamers have long been known to book time off work for major releases.
When Red Dead Redemption 2 launched in October 2018, social media users were sharing plans to take the day off, with one analytics firm reportedly finding , external more people talking about calling in sick for it than any other game that year.
Similar conversations took place ahead of Cyberpunk 2077's release in December 2020, with fans discussing , external taking several days off to play.
GTA 6 is set in a fictional state inspired by Florida, which has featured heavily in the game's marketing, including this promotional blimp.
Some places have decided to lean into the trend for GTA 6 by offering incentives around the game - including the US Army's 3rd Infantry Division based at Fort Stewart, Georgia.
It gave some active-duty soldiers a four-day pass to play the game when it is released in November, as long as they sign a reenlistment contract for a minimum of two years between 1 August and 12 November.
"The idea was to have a unique incentives programme that connects to what soldiers are interested in," public affairs officer for the division, Lieutenant Colonel Angel Tomko confirmed to the BBC in August.
"There are 130 soldiers eligible within the battalion, and 20 have selected this incentive as part of their reenlistment," she said at the time.
This article contains content provided by Instagram.  We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies.  You may want to read Metaâs Instagram cookie policy , external and privacy policy , external before accepting. To view this content choose âaccept and continueâ .
Aside from taking time off, some gamers have also been discussing a technical loophole which could give them valuable extra hours of play before it officially unlocks in their country.
Because GTA 6 will release at midnight local time in all regions, New Zealand will become one of the first places where it is available, due to it reaching midnight earliest because of its position near the international date line.
This has led to some investigating ways to "trick" their consoles into thinking they're based in the island country when they are in fact thousands of miles away.
According to Google Trends, searches for the "GTA 6 New Zealand trick" have surged by more than 5,000% in the UK over the past month.
Games journalist Vic Hood said many gamers would be looking to play earlier to "get in on the action as soon as possible", as well as to prevent spoilers.
"As New Zealand is 13 hours ahead of the UK, that's 13 hours of gameplay that has time to spread across the internet and potentially spoil some key story beats and in-game surprises," she said.
"Took an extra day of paid time off when I found this out," one fan posted on Reddit on the trick.
It also means gamers would be playing the game at the much nicer time of 11:00 GMT, rather than having to stay up all night.
But another Xbox user shared caution on Reddit, noting that while the loophole had been exploited for many years for other game releases, GTA 6 "might be the game where Microsoft finally does something about this 'exploit'" - which could include  banning players.
GTA 6's developers Rockstar and publishers Take Two Interactive have not commented on the loophole, and neither have Sony nor Microsoft.
Louise Wooldridge from Ampere Analysis said both Microsoft and Sony had "rules governing regional accounts and purchases" for the Xbox and PlayStation, adding that Sony's were "slightly more restrictive".
Players who choose to use the workaround could therefore risk breaching those terms and conditions and potentially face restrictions on their accounts or lose access to their digital games.
The hype for the game has taken over locations across the world, including Selfridges in London
Some gamers will have to wait even longer than their console-playing counterparts to get their hands on GTA 6, as the game will not be available on PC at launch, similar to previous GTA releases.
"Spare a thought for the PC users who will have to live vicariously through others' YouTube videos and Twitch streams," gamer Stephen Finn told the BBC.
A PS5 now costs from Â£520, while the more powerful PS5 Pro is nearly Â£790.
Despite the hefty price tag, for some the temptation to join the community in playing what many have called the biggest game launch of the year, if not decade, has been too great.
Reddit posts and videos, such as one by US YouTuber isoish , external , show fans buying consoles specifically to play the game.
"So, the only game I'm going to have on here is GTA," the content creator said in the video.
"The whole PS5 is for GTA 6."
After more than a decade of waiting, it seems some fans are determined not to waste a single minute of GTA 6's release - no matter the cost or extra effort.

articles.title_orig: Xbox's Project Helix "is not a PC that can also play console games"
articles.title_zh: Xbox's Project Helix "is not a PC that can also play console games"
articles.content_orig:
Xbox VP of Next Generation Jason Ronald has clarified that Project Helix is "designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games, not a PC that can also play console games."
In the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine , Ronald described Project Helix as "the ultimate gaming machine – one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed."
"The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it."
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed Project Helix's console and PC compatibility in March, adding that the console will "lead in performance" for Xbox and PC games.
As Ronald previously discussed at GDC Festival of Gaming , Project Helix will utilise neural rendering, which uses AI models to enhance graphics. Ronald identified neural rendering as a particular focus for Project Helix, as it also addresses the ongoing component crisis.
"It's definitely a challenging time, but as a system and platform designer, it's one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also [making] things accessible and affordable."
"This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower [and] additional memory."
He concluded: "I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last ten years."
Reports last month indicated that Project Helix is expected to launch during the 2028 holiday season , with a projected price between $1,200 and $1,800.

articles.title_orig: Can Google win the AI race without killing its cash cow? : Planet Money
articles.title_zh: Can Google win the AI race without killing its cash cow? : Planet Money
articles.content_orig:
Plain English With Derek Thompson
For roughly 25 years, the economics of the web were pretty straightforward. Publishers created information, Google indexed it, users searched Google, Google sent those users to those publishers’ websites, and the publishers monetized those visits with advertising. But last month, the stock of Alphabet, the parent company of Google, plunged nearly $500 billion when the company flagged to investors that the firm would use more AI in its search.
The rise of AI doesn’t just threaten to disrupt Google; it threatens to destroy the economics of web publishing. With AI, Google doesn’t just direct our attention to the answer; it now answers the question entirely. For many publishers that live and die on search traffic and clicks, this shift is existential. News websites are shuttering, journalism layoffs are rising, and even Wikipedia reported that human page views have fallen by almost 10 percent in the last year. Artificial intelligence is very much threatening to change the business model of the internet as we understand it, and an internet that runs on chatbots is going to require a totally new set of economic rules.
Subscribe to our YouTube channel here .
If you have questions, observations, or ideas for future episodes, email us at PlainEnglish@Spotify.com.
In the following excerpt, Derek and Joe Marchese get into why Google is leaning into AI search and what it means for the rest of the internet.
Derek Thompson: Let’s start with the news. Alphabet lost more than half a trillion in market value after its latest earnings report, which really freaked out investors, as it seems like the company’s going to allow AI searches to eat into overall searches. I think a lot of people are thinking, “OK, well, AI searches often give you answers rather than just lists of links.”
I thought the whole business model of Google was clicking on one of those links. Why is Google seeming, at least, to risk the destruction of the greatest business model in history?
Joe Marchese: I think the very simple answer is it has no choice. If you look at Google’s mission statement, it’s to organize the world’s information and make it universally accessible and useful. Very important, that last part. AI is a lot of things, but what it certainly is is better search. And maybe to put a finer point on it, it’s better search results because it synthesizes a lot of information from a lot of different places and brings answers. They’re not perfect, getting better all the time. So if you said, “Our mission is to organize the world’s information, make it universally accessible and useful,” AI is that.
And here’s a fun fact that I think some of your listeners might know, but maybe not. The paper that kicked off the ChatGPT revolution is called “Attention Is All You Need,” because they were teaching neural networks to learn very similar to attention models. The people who wrote that paper all worked at Google.
All of them, except for, I think, there was one person from the University of Toronto. So good on University of Toronto for getting in there. So why did Google have all those engineers that wrote the paper that kicked off ChatGPT and didn’t launch ChatGPT? So I think it’s easy to say this wasn’t Google’s first choice to get into an arms race for the new search engine, but now it has no choice.
Thompson: It’s not just that answers are replacing search. It’s also that click-through rates are dying at a rapid pace, which completely changes the business model for publishers. In the open that I just recorded, there was a study that Pew did that tracked about 68,000 Google searches. And when an AI overview appears at the top of the results page, the click-through rate declines by half, and only 1 percent, only 1 in 100 users, actually click a cited source in that AI overview. Is this as simple as the click is dying?
Marchese: I mean, yes is the answer. I mean, you look at what click-through rates are on other chatbots, on ChatGPT or Claude. The information is coming to people rather than people going out onto the web. And let me be clear: I think Google will absolutely be fine. The fact that it had half a trillion dollars to lose in a day and is still a multitrillion-dollar business because it’s diversified into YouTube and Waymo and servers and chips, but everything downstream of Google is having its business model reevaluated. And you know what’s downstream of Google? The entire internet. And so that is the question we’re at right now.
Thompson: And what is the beginning of the answer? I mean, what is your counsel to publishers, to creators, to people running an internet business when you’re saying that the click is dying?
Thompson: Where does one begin to see some optimism here?
Marchese: Well, some optimism comes from: New, fresh information becomes more valuable than ever. The joke of: How does information get from meat world into AI? How does it learn that the coffee shop down the street is the best? Something has to be feeding this thing. The problem is we have a bit of a gap between now and whatever the new model is going to be, which is just that Indiana Jones trying to swap out the treasure with a bag of sand before it goes—and people always use that example, and they forget he didn’t pull it off. The boulder came after him.
Thompson: No, the boulder comes right after him. Yeah.
Marchese: So the problem is, and actually you see Cloudflare probably has some of the best stats on this and the work they’re doing to try to protect publishers and create a marketplace for the value of their content, but people don’t realize advertising is what made up so much of the revenue. This AI arms race is actually being fueled by ad revenue from Google, from Meta, from Amazon. And so if we replace that, and the publishers aren’t getting traffic to their sites, subscription will matter more than ever, fresh content will matter more than ever, and then protecting it and getting a fair share from the hyperscalers for reading their information.
This excerpt has been edited and condensed.

articles.title_orig: US government confirms investigation into tech firm Megaspeed
articles.title_zh: US government confirms investigation into tech firm Megaspeed
articles.content_orig:
The United States has confirmed it is investigating computing company Megaspeed, suspecting it of violating US export controls by helping to ship tech giant Nvidia's chips to China.
In a joint statement, the US Department of Justice and Department of Commerce said they had been investigating Singapore-based firm Megaspeed since 2024.
It comes after questions were raised about the possibility high-end AI chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.
Concerns emerged in recent weeks after Nvidia founder Jensen Huang revealed he had an extramarital affair , allegedly with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. US authorities suspect her of spying for Beijing, which China denies.
Jensen Huang resigned from his role as chief executive last week following revelations he had two affairs.
Megaspeed is the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in South East Asia and is suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China. The Singapore-based company said on Sunday it had launched an internal investigation into its business.
The justice and commerce departments said on Monday that "it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information" regarding the investigation.
Laying out a timeline, it said it began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 "for potential export control violations".
In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia "concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed". In June 2025, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its 'no sell' list.
Agents from the Bureau of Industry and Security, in conjunction with Singaporean law enforcement officials, then conducted an on-site check at Megaspeed that month and interviewed Alice Huang, who was chief executive at the time.
Alice Huang and Jensen Huang pictured together in Taiwan in June 2024
Following this enforcement action, the Department of Justice took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed.
The Nvidia scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end chips to Megaspeed.
On Friday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed the US Commerce Department, led by Howard Lutnick, for failing to properly oversee the export of the chips.
Lutnick has been called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over his department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips.
While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls.
Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair.
The White House said on Monday it would further restrict China's access to AI chips from firms like Nvidia.
The reported affairs by Jensen Huang created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a major company in the AI industry and central to the US as it competes with China for dominance.
Trump downplays warnings of AI risks, citing rivalry with China
In the statement, the US government said it would "bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred".
They added: "Sensitive technologies like semiconductors are among the most valuable and strategic assets of the US economy, and the Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce will remain vigilant in pursuing justice for those who want to compromise America's technological edge."

articles.title_orig: Home Depot taps Richard McPhail as new CEO, reports Q3 earnings beat
articles.title_zh: Home Depot taps Richard McPhail as new CEO, reports Q3 earnings beat
articles.content_orig:
Home Depot on Tuesday announced its Chief Financial Officer Richard McPhail will become CEO of the company, replacing Ted Decker, effective next week.
Alongside McPhail's appointment, Home Depot said Ann-Marie Campbell, currently senior executive vice president of U.S. stores and operations, will become president and chief operating officer. Jordan Broggi has been chosen as CFO to replace McPhail.
Decker, CEO since 2022, had been on temporary medical leave since August. The company said on Tuesday that Decker has returned from leave but is now stepping down from his role. He will continue to serve as chair of the board of directors, the company said.
"I'm glad to be back and grateful for the support I received," Decker told analysts on Tuesday. "The board and I have agreed that now is the right time to move to the next phase of our succession plan."
McPhail has been with the company since 2005, holding multiple executive roles.
"We're not going to change course," McPhail told CNBC's Becky Quick.
He said the company will continue to lean into winning professional shoppers like contractors and using AI tools to encourage sales. McPhail added that while the company faces more challenges now than it did at the start of the year, it is still winning share of the home improvement market.
Home Depot has been pressured by a sluggish housing market, higher mortgage rates and a more cautious consumer. Still, the company has previously said it's seen resilience among its pro shoppers who are still shopping for their home improvement projects.
Shares of Home Depot sank more than 3% following the announcement and the retailer's fiscal third-quarter results.
The CEO change came as the home improvement retailer posted quarterly  earnings and revenue that beat analysts' expectations. The company said comparable sales rose 2.2% during the period, compared with estimates of up 1.8%, according to StreetAccount.
Here's how Home Depot performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
The company reported net income of $3.71 billion, or $3.72 per share, compared with $3.60 billion, or $3.62 per share, the year prior. Excluding one-time items, Home Depot reported adjusted earnings per share of $3.86.
Revenue rose 4.9% compared to the year-ago period.
"We also are confident that we are taking material share from the market and from competition," McPhail said on the call with analysts.
In the third quarter, the company said online comparable sales grew around 13%, which marked its sixth straight quarter of double-digit positive growth for the metric.
The company said it saw positive comparable sales numbers in 13 out of 16 of its merchandising departments, including notable strength in the power department, which posted double-digit percentage growth.
For the full year, Home Depot said it expects total sales to rise roughly 4.5%, the top end of its previously provided range. It also anticipates comparable sales will grow around 1.4%, compared with an outlook of flat to a 2% increase.
Home Depot added it expects adjusted earnings per share to rise 2% this year, compared with prior guidance of flat to a 4% increase.

articles.title_orig: Cyber Attack Hits 178 Major Websites: Full List of Affected Organizations
articles.title_zh: Cyber Attack Hits 178 Major Websites: Full List of Affected Organizations
articles.content_orig:
Christian Hudspeth , Logistics Coordinator
Hackers used a security vulnerability in a popular website software platform to target visitors to some of the world’s largest websites, attempting to steal financial information, cryptocurrency and infect iPhones, according to cybersecurity researchers.
The attack affected websites associated with at least 178 organizations, including Zoom, CNN, Equifax, HSBC, Salesforce, IKEA and Peacock, according to an investigation published Monday by cybersecurity researcher Scott Helme and his company, Report URI .
Researchers identified 188 infected JavaScript files after examining 1,611 files associated with Optimizely, a platform businesses use to test and customize their websites.
The attack involved malicious code distributed through a trusted third-party service rather than hackers necessarily breaking into each affected company’s systems.
According to Report URI’s investigation, the malicious software was designed to carry out several types of attacks, including:
Researchers identified two exploit kits targeting Apple’s iOS operating system, known as Coruna and DarkSword.
Report URI also identified cryptocurrency transactions involving wallets associated with the attackers, indicating that some cryptocurrency had been stolen. However, the full financial impact of the incident remains unclear.
The attack exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely’s Web Experimentation platform, which allows businesses to customize website content and test different versions of webpages.
According to Report URI, attackers inserted malicious JavaScript into a feature that allows customers to add their own code.
Because the modified scripts were delivered through Optimizely’s legitimate infrastructure, visitors could encounter malicious code while browsing familiar websites.
The researchers traced the earliest identified malicious script to Nov. 16 at 4:21 a.m. UTC.
By later that day, researchers found that nearly all the previously identified infected scripts had been cleaned up.
Optimizely acknowledged the security incident in an official update posted to its service status page .
The company confirmed that an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation platform to insert malicious JavaScript into certain customer projects.
Optimizely said it had fixed the vulnerability, removed the injected code, taken steps to secure affected accounts and introduced additional protections to prevent unauthorized code from being delivered.
The company continued monitoring the incident as of its Nov. 17 update.
KPRC 2 has reached out to Optimizely for more information.
Several companies responded to the incident following inquiries from Reuters and KPRC 2.
Salesforce told Reuters it was investigating unauthorized changes involving Optimizely scripts and had disabled the scripts as a precaution.
In a statement to KPRC 2, Equifax said they have stopped using Optimizely after investigating the incident.
Equifax is aware of reports that Optimizely, a digital experience platform commonly used for website testing, has identified and blocked a security issue targeting the Optimizely Experimentation Platform. We immediately investigated this issue and ceased our use of Optimizely. We have not identified evidence of any compromise to our systems or impact to our data. Few companies have invested more time and resources than Equifax to ensure that consumers’ information is protected, as evidenced by our more than $3 billion security and technology transformation.
Zoom said it had also ceased operations with Optimizely as a precaution.
“As a precautionary measure, Zoom has disabled Optimizely across our production environments. At this time, we have not identified any impact to customer data. We continue to monitor the situation closely,” Zoom said in their online Trust Center .
IKEA told Reuters it was investigating whether the incident had affected its digital services or customers.
KPRC 2 is reaching out to more organizations.
Although researchers confirmed that malicious scripts were delivered through affected websites, the number of people whose devices or personal information were compromised remains unknown.
Reuters reported that it could not independently determine the full extent of any successful attacks.
Report URI’s findings indicate that cryptocurrency theft occurred, but they do not establish that every website visitor was affected or that every attempted attack succeeded.
The presence of malicious code on a website also does not necessarily mean the company’s internal systems were breached.
Anyone concerned about potential exposure can take several precautions:
Simply visiting one of the affected websites does not establish that a person’s device or information was compromised.

Ajay Patel joined KPRC 2 in July 2026 after reporting at LEX 18 in Lexington, Kentucky, where he covered major breaking news and disasters. A Delaware native and Temple University grad, he’s a Rookie of the Year award finalist who enjoys golf, the gym, and hunting for Houston’s best dessert spots.
Christian Hudspeth is a Houston native who joined KPRC 2 News in December 2025. Christian began his news career at KTRK in 2022 before moving to newsrooms in Waco, Texas (KXXV), Las Vegas, Nevada (KTNV), and now back to H-Town. He earned his BA at the University of Houston Jack J. Valenti School of Communication in 2023.

articles.title_orig: Carney and Xi Announce Trade Pact Ahead of Asia Summit
articles.title_zh: Carney and Xi Announce Trade Pact Ahead of Asia Summit
articles.content_orig:
President Trump speaks to members of the media on the South Lawn of the White House on Nov. 16, 2026, ahead of a fraught meeting this week with President Xi Jinping of China where A.I. chips could be a key issue.
The Trump administration on Monday announced it was tightening a loophole that has allowed Chinese tech firms to bypass U.S. restrictions on accessing the most advanced A.I. chips through third countries.
The move comes just days ahead of President Trump’s meeting this week with Chinese President Xi Jinping, and in the wake of Nvidia, the creator of the most advanced AI chips, becoming enmeshed in an international scandal that prompted the resignation of CEO and President Jensen Huang and a fresh round of scrutiny over the company’s ties to China.
The new rule released by the Commerce Department will require that buyers of advanced semiconductors from certain countries will need to secure a license to sell or transfer those chips.The administration said the rule would specifically impact buyers from Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil, describing those countries as having a “higher than normal” risk of evading current sanctions.
The measure is set to go into effect in 90 days.
China is currently barred from purchasing certain advanced chips directly from U.S.-based companies like Nvidia. Yet some Chinese companies have circumvented the rules by either purchasing the chips through shell companies in third countries, or renting computing powers among data centers located in countries where the U.S. hasn’t restricted on chip exports.
The new rule will also give Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick wide discretion as to which chips may require more safeguards. According to the rules, the secretary may inform a company selling AI chips “orally” about stricter export rules on certain items if the department believes there is “an unacceptable risk.”
The rules came days after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized Lutnick for failing to properly oversee the chip exports to China in a CNBC interview on Sunday.
The rare public criticism came after Huang’s resignation as head of Nvidia in the wake of revelations about his extramarital affairs, including a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect of spying for China. Megaspeed is suspected by the Commerce Department of diverting Nvidia chips to China in violation of U.S. export controls, but a month-long investigation by the Commerce Department into Megaspeed was halted last year after a top Nvidia official intervened , according to the New York Times.
“Treasury, War, USTR and State were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months,” Bessent said on CNBC on Sunday. “But Commerce has the pen, and you will have to ask them about their internal processes.”
“President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s, so any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts our great companies in the AI race, because it gives the Chinese an advantage,” Bessent added.
Both Lutnick and Bessent are expected to travel with Trump to China this week, according to Semafor. Trump is scheduled to arrive in China on Wednesday to meet with both Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. Aside from AI chips, the first-of-its-kind summit will also focus on the reduction of nuclear weapons.
The federal government began restricting China's access to AI chips in Trump's first term, as both countries raced to become the leader  in this fast-evolving technology. The Biden administration intensified this policy , making the export of advanced chips to China illegal in 2022. Beijing nevertheless still succeeded in stockpiling thousands of chips to build its own AI systems thanks to an international smuggling network.
Last year, Trump reversed his own administration’s export restrictions, allowing Nvidia to sell two types of computer chip used in the development of artificial intelligence to "approved customers" in China in exchange for a portion of the revenue cut. Those moves are poised to draw more scrutiny next year when Democrats take control of Congress, with both chambers likely probing the Trump Administration's AI policies in the wake of the Nvidia scandal. Congressional lawmakers have asked the Commerce Department to preserve all records related to Nvidia as a part of the investigation.

articles.title_orig: Trump admin. unveils new rule to deny China's access to U.S. AI chips
articles.title_zh: Trump admin. unveils new rule to deny China's access to U.S. AI chips
articles.content_orig:
United States President Donald Trump’s administration has announced new restrictions on China’s access to advanced chips amid fallout from the alleged spy scandal involving AI giant Nvidia.
The rule announced by the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) on Monday aims to prevent Chinese AI developers from getting around export controls by remotely accessing data centres in third countries, particularly in Southeast Asia.
It designates Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil as countries with an “unacceptable risk of diversion” and requires anyone seeking to ship advanced chips to those destinations to obtain an export licence.
BIS, which sits under the Department of Commerce, said the change was a “logical extension” of the existing requirement for companies to obtain a licence to export or transfer chips to firms based in China.
“The United States is the global leader in advanced computing and super intelligence technology and is committed to promoting the global adoption of American technology for legitimate commercial purposes while ensuring that sensitive technologies are not exploited in ways that threaten US national security,” BIS said in a statement.
While Chinese firms are barred from importing the most advanced graphics processing units (GPUs) under US export controls, they had until now been legally able to take advantage of remote access to top-of-the-line computing power at data centres in countries such as Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand.
Singapore, which hosts dozens of data centres, said on Tuesday that it was “studying the details of this new measure carefully”.
“We are engaging affected companies to understand the potential impact on their businesses,” the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry and the Ministry of Digital Development and Information said in a joint statement.
“We have also been engaging the relevant US authorities on the scope and implementation of the measure, as well as exploring how to facilitate trusted access for Singapore companies.”
The ministries added that they did not condone companies using Singapore to “circumvent or violate” the laws of other countries.
The restrictions come as Nvidia’s export of advanced chips is under scrutiny following claims that former CEO Jensen Huang was romantically involved with a woman recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security for espionage.
Huang, who became one of the most prominent faces of the AI boom at the helm of Nvidia, resigned last week amid a company board investigation into allegations involving the Chinese-born executive of Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed.
Beijing has denied the spying allegations, made by unnamed US officials in media reports, calling them “entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China”.
Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive identified as Jensen Huang’s ex-romantic partner, has not publicly commented on the claims.
Late on Monday, the US Commerce Department and the Department of Justice publicly confirmed that investigators had opened a criminal investigation into Megaspeed.
The Commerce Department began investigating Megaspeed for potential export control violations in 2024, leading BIS officials to conduct an on-site inspection of the Singapore-based company and to interview Alice Huang the following year, the statement said.
The Justice Department subsequently took the “lead role” in the criminal investigation, according to the statement.
“The Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security working together will bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred,” it said.
US tech stocks fell sharply on Monday as investors weighed the scandal’s fallout on the AI rollout.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 2.5 percent, closing in the red for the third consecutive session.
The broader S&P 500 dropped 1.9 percent.
Shares of Nvidia, which have shed more than 30 percent of their market value over the past month, dropped 4.1 percent.
The other six companies of the “Magnificent Seven” also lost ground, with Alphabet and Amazon seeing the next-biggest declines of 4.1 percent and 3.3 percent, respectively.
The sell-off continued in Asia on Tuesday, with key indexes in Japan, South Korea and Hong Kong closing in the red.
Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 and South Korea’s Kospi closed down 1.3 percent and 2.6 percent, respectively, while the Hang Seng Index in Hong Kong dropped 0.9 percent.

articles.title_orig: Trump says he may meet with N. Korean leader in China
articles.title_zh: Trump says he may meet with N. Korean leader in China
articles.content_orig:
Trump's trip comes amid the Nvidia CEO scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy.
President Donald Trump is traveling to Asia for meetings with global leaders and for his second visit to China for a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
As he departed the White House Monday morning, Trump said he "may" meet with North Korea's Kim Jong Un in China as well, though he said it would ultimately be Xi's decision.
"He may come. I don't know. That's up to President Xi," Trump said of Kim Jong Un.
Trump will participate in the first-ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia on the sidelines of the APEC Summit in China, senior U.S. officials said. The president is expected to discuss the war in Iran with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin. However, he does not intend to discuss Ukraine during the trilateral meeting, officials say.
Denuclearization will be the focus of the long-awaited trilateral meeting, though officials said they do not anticipate the leaders reaching any concrete agreement and are characterizing this meeting as an initial conversation broaching the subject.
Trump had been teasing a potential face-to-face meeting with the world's leading nuclear superpowers for some time. On Oct. 19, Trump told ABC News Chief White House correspondent Mary Bruce that he would like to meet with Putin and Xi when he visits China, saying "I would do that," and indicated a desire to discuss denuclearization.
Trump and Xi will have a bilateral meeting ahead of the trilateral, though Trump and Putin will not be meeting one-on-one separately, the officials said.
The president's trip comes as questions linger about what the administration knew about prominent tech CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.
Billionaire Elon Musk will be joining Trump for parts of his China travels. Officials did not specify his reason for accompanying the president, merely pointing to Musk's business interests in China.
An official said they expect some additional U.S. business leaders to be attending the APEC CEO Summit, but clarified that they are not part of the U.S. delegation.
Trump is expected to leave Washington in the morning of Monday, Nov. 16 and arrive in Manila in the evening of Tuesday, Nov. 17, and will head to a bilateral meeting with the other members of the Quad, a diplomatic partnership the U.S. has with Australia, India, and Japan, about peace and security in the Indo-Pacific region. The president is also expected to sign a trade deal with Thailand.
He will then participate in an ASEAN cocktail reception followed by a summit dinner.
The next day, Trump will participate in a welcome ceremony at Malacañang Presidential Palace, the official residence of Filipino President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Romualdez Marcos Jr., followed by a bilateral meeting. He will also participate in an Association of Southeast Asian Nations cocktail reception followed by a summit dinner.
After Wednesday’s events in the Philippines, Trump travels to Shenzhen, China, where it is expected that a minister will greet Trump on the tarmac. He will participate in an APEC leaders' dinner and multilateral meeting with the APEC leaders. On Thursday afternoon local time, Trump will participate in a bilateral meeting and working lunch with Chinese President Xi.
The historic trilateral Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting will be the final event on the president's Asia swing.
Each of Trump and Xi’s meetings this year have been clouded by other topics.
When Trump visited China in May, the raging war in Iran overshadowed the state visit that was scheduled after a detente in Trump's tit-for-tat trade war. Also, when Trump welcomed Xi in September, the pomp and circumstance Trump had planned went without live TV coverage after his banning outlets from the press pool led to a network boycott.
Now, in the background of this trip, is the scandal involving Nvidia's CEO, Huang, who joined Trump's last trip to China earlier this year after boarding Air Force One during a refueling stop in Alaska, according to pool reports at the time. Huang was reported to have had an affair with Alice Huang , a Chinese national and tech executive who is accused of being a Chinese spy.
Officials said they do not expect Trump to raise the allegations against Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese spy, with President Xi, adding that the two presidents plan to focus on implementing aspects of their trade agreement.
"You know, I think when it comes to some of these national security matters and examinations and investigations that are going on in the U.S., it's probably not something that we're going to read the Chinese in on at this moment," a senior U.S. official said.
Huang resigned from Nvidia's board and as its president and CEO on Nov. 12.
This scandal engulfing Huang has introduced scrutiny over Trump’s ties to him and what Trump and other administration officials knew about the relationship with the alleged spy.
"Well, I've been hearing about it and I've been reading a little bit about it over a period of time. But, not too long ago," Trump told reporters during an impromptu press conference in the White House briefing room on Nov. 9.
When pressed on if he was aware of the allegations during his May trip to China, Trump said: "No, I didn't hear about it then. But a lot of people have heard about it, and Jensen totally denies that he had."
On May 12, Secretary of State Marco Rubio shared intelligence with Trump on Air Force One showing Huang was in a relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy, a U.S. official and two sources familiar with the matter told ABC News. This is the second known time that Trump had been warned about the plot. Trump was briefed by Rubio shortly before Huang was set to join Trump on the trip to China, the U.S. official and sources said.
A U.S. official and a source familiar with the matter told ABC News that after Air Force One landed in China, White House officials asked for business leaders -- including Huang -- to be allowed into a meeting with President Xi. Initially, the Chinese were hesitant to adjust the program, but ultimately agreed to it.
Huang, who co-founded Nvidia, one of the world’s most-valuable companies and the maker of chips that top AI companies heavily rely on, has been a constant presence around Trump, who has invited tech executives to multiple events, both at the White House and on overseas trips. Since April 28, when Huang and his wife, Lori, attended a state dinner for King Charles III and Queen Camila, the tech CEO has participated in at least six events with Trump, including the September state dinner for Xi.
Huang has lobbied for policy positions that benefit China and Chinese companies over the past few months.
For example, the U.S. has long blocked China's access to American AI chips. However, in December 2025, after lobbying from Huang, Trump loosened those restrictions -- approving the sale of some older but still powerful chips to China as part of a remarkable deal that gave the U.S. government a 25% cut of the sales.
And in July of this year, Huang joined the social media platform X to push back against possible bans on open-weight AI models, the type that Chinese companies have embraced, and which would be cheaper for businesses and governments to adopt. The ban would benefit American companies OpenAI and Anthropic, which use closed models. The U.S. was reportedly considering those bans.
"The world needs both frontier closed models and frontier open models," Huang wrote in his first-ever X post.

articles.title_zh: Apec and Asean summits live: protests await Trump in Manila, as Xi greets leaders in Shenzhen
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Taiwan is likely to be overshadowed as presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump are expected to meet on the sidelines of the Asia Pacific Economic Forum this week, even as the threat from China evolves and grows stronger.
Leaders from China, the U.S. and some 21 other economies will gather at the APEC summit this week in Shenzhen, China. Recent events like the scandal that forced Nvidia's CEO to resign, export controls and the ongoing trade dispute have made the tech competition between Beijing and Washington all the more pressing.
Few expect major breakthroughs on Taiwan, a self-ruled island that is claimed by Beijing. While the U.S. does not formally recognize Taiwan, it is the island’s biggest informal ally and seller of arms.
“For the Trump administration, this isn’t a core issue between the U.S. and China,” said Arthur Zhin-Sheng Wang, an expert on cross-Straits relations at Taiwan’s Central Police University.
US-Taiwan ties remain strong behind the scenes
Experts largely say that cooperation with the U.S. remains strong below the level of rhetoric, despite Trump’s public ambivalence toward Taiwan.
One sign of this came from the summer, when the de facto United States embassy in Taiwan posted a photo showing joint patrols between the two coast guards, a rare occurrence, as the U.S. does not usually acknowledge it has direct cooperation with Taiwan in any defense capacity.
“This also is proof of the decades that Taiwan and U.S. have had of cooperation and training. I was also surprised,” said Kuo Yu-jen, a defense studies expert and director of the Institute for National Policy Research in Taiwan.
The U.S. is obligated by law to help Taiwan defend itself, which has manifested in the form of arms sales, while the government officially adopts a stance of ambiguity on whether it would intervene militarily in the case of a Chinese invasion.
The Taiwanese public is used to the continued uncertainties of the island’s relationship with the U.S. Research from the Institute of National Defense and Security Research in Taiwan, a government-funded think tank, showed that public attitudes toward the U.S. remain around the same. Polls conducted in the past five years show that about half of the public believes the U.S. will send soldiers to support Taiwan in the event of a Chinese invasion, and about half don’t.
“I do think they will take some actions, though it may not be sending soldiers,” said Allen Hsieh, a 28-year-old media professional in Taipei. “I think Taiwan’s importance to the U.S. is even more important than Ukraine.”
Stalled arms sales for now
Since starting his second term, Trump called for Taiwan to spend more on its own defense and Taiwan responded that it would commit to 5% of its GDP on defense.
Arms sales are ongoing. While much media attention has focused on a $14 billion package that remains stalled, an earlier package of $11 billion approved at the end of last year is in progress. Some of the stalled arms packages have been delayed since before Trump came into office, experts have also said.
Those include fighter jets. Taiwan received the first two of long-delayed F-16V fighter jets from the U.S. in October, and three more jets earlier this month. The aircraft are a part of a long list of backlogged U.S. orders worth almost $30 billion, according to the Taiwan Security Monitor research project which tracks defense-related developments on the island at George Mason University.
But the delays are not necessarily because of political considerations with China, a concern that was raised when Trump said he discussed arms sales with Xi earlier this year. Instead, it may be more of an issue with manufacturing capacity, particularly for future sales.
Congress approved the sale of long-range precision strike systems to Taiwan in December 2025, but Taiwan faces competition because of limited supplies. Kuo noted that among the missiles approved for sale are the same ones being used by the U.S. military in the ongoing Iran war, such as the HIMARS rockets and supplies were low.
“I don’t think this is a political issue. They just can’t produce so many of these missiles in a short period,” he said.
China expands coast guard role in pressure on Taiwan
Meanwhile, China has intensified its military and nonmilitary pressure on Taiwan. In 2025, the People’s Liberation Army flew about 5,448 fighter jet sorties toward the island during military exercises, according to Skyfaring, an open-source website that compiles public data from Taiwan’s Ministry of Defense. That marked a sharp increase from the years before 2023, when such flights were sporadic.
Beijing also recently held unannounced military drills in the Western Pacific, deploying more than 100 vessels in waters near Taiwan and Japan, Taiwan’s National Security Council chief Joseph Wu said in a Nov. 3 post on X.
The number of PLA flights recorded this year stood at 2,401 as of Nov. 12, below the full-year total for 2025.
“I think the threat is transforming ... for example, more of its exercises are now about blockading and sealing off” Taiwan, Wang said, rather than firing live missiles. He said Beijing was expanding its gray-zone tactics — aggressive actions that fall short of open warfare.
These include greater use of the coast guard to assert China’s claims, mirroring its approach elsewhere. In June, the Chinese coast guard began patrolling off Taiwan’s east coast, which faces the open Pacific, extending its activities beyond Taiwan’s outlying islands closer to China.
Wang compared the approach to Beijing’s tactics in the South China Sea, where Chinese coast guard vessels patrol waters disputed with the Philippines. China has also designated a shoal claimed by the Philippines as a nature reserve under Chinese protection.
“It’s telling the whole world it has sovereignty here.”

articles.title_orig: Trump Administration Tightens AI Chip Export Restrictions Ahead of China Visit
articles.title_zh: Trump Administration Tightens AI Chip Export Restrictions Ahead of China Visit
articles.content_orig:
Sen. Maria Cantwell , the top Democrat on the Senate commerce committee, alleged in a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Sunday that the department under his leadership failed to prevent China from accessing the U.S.'s most advanced artificial intelligence chips.
In the letter, Cantwell prodded Lutnick to enforce export controls and stop the flow of AI chips to companies barred from receiving the technology. She sent the missive ahead of a planned meeting this week between U.S. officials and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, in China.
Her urging comes as Washington reels from revelations that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang. Nvidia is the leading U.S. company designing advanced AI chips.
Alice Huang was an executive at Singaporean technology company Megaspeed that allegedly smuggled restricted chips to China.
Lutnick, meanwhile, has come under fire for stalling efforts to crack down on chip sales to China and for his close personal relationship with Jensen Huang, who was a vocal opponent of export controls.
"The Department of Commerce has resisted efforts to restrict companies flagged as national security threats, weakened safeguards, and left open pathways for the PRC to train advanced AI models using sensitive American technology," Cantwell wrote to Lutnick. "These failures to carry out the law help give away America's technology advantage in AI."
The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Monday.
Cantwell called on Lutnick to use his authority to enforce a 2018 law, known as the Export Control Reform Act , which gives the Commerce Department broad latitude to enforce export controls and protect sensitive American technology.
She also cites potential financial conflicts involving Lutnick's sons , who control Cantor Fitzgerald, which she said held $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock at the time of his nomination. And she notes the Trump administration's 25% fee on certain Nvidia chips sold to China, which she said could create "a perverse financial incentive to approve exports of sensitive American technology."
"America's national security and AI leadership cannot be compromised by family business interests or a policy that generates federal revenue from exporting technology critical to our competitive edge," Cantwell wrote.
Both Democratic and Republican members of Congress have ramped up pressure on Lutnick and other Commerce Department officials after a Nov. 9 New York Times report alleging the department may have slow-walked an investigation into Megaspeed.
On Thursday, Senate banking committee Chair Tim Scott , R-S.C., summoned both Huang and Lutnick t o testify before his committee in December.
Lutnick has agreed to appear before the panel, Kristen Eichamer, a Commerce Department spokesperson, said in a statement last week.
And Democrats, who will take control of both the House and Senate in January, have signaled they will investigate Jensen Huang and Commerce officials.
On Wednesday, Sen. Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., the top Democrat on the Senate banking panel, and Sen. Chris Coons , D-Del., the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations subpanel with jurisdiction over East Asia and the Pacific, sent a letter to Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller instructing them to preserve all documents and communications related to Nvidia's exports of "advanced AI chips to China or to entities that may divert such chips to China."
The letter gives all three officials until Nov. 17 to confirm that preservation directives have been issued.
